# Tesla extraction baseline

This fixture captures the **unchanged legacy Tesla pipeline** before framework
refactoring. It is not a VehicleRecon3D implementation or a generic-pipeline pass.

- `output_manifest.json`: all 91 original delivered file identities, verified
  against both `Tesla.zip` and the workspace at source commit `5dad4d9`.
- `delivered/`: original validation metrics, masks, screenshots, dimensions,
  Blender source, GLB, export metadata and full scene inventory.
- `rerun/`: corresponding outputs regenerated by the unchanged archive scripts
  in an isolated working copy, plus execution logs and output identities.
- `comparison.json`: machine-checked old/new metrics, geometry and scene
  comparison; records differences without requiring byte-identical assets.
- `script_inventory.json`: 20 executable script classifications, 52 named Python
  function locations/classes and the declared coupling-unit counts.
- `MANIFEST.sha256`: identities of all files in this fixture except itself.

All four IoUs and every view metric reproduce exactly: side .957230, top .936083,
front .931202, rear .944724. Acceptance floors remain .94/.92/.92/.90.
Geometry audit, direct GLB comparison, browser QA and exact embedded GLB checks
pass. Geometry contains 191 exported mesh nodes and 245,952 triangles. The 262
scene objects retain the same IDs, transforms and control geometry/curves.

One presentation-state difference: original STUDIO_GROUND.hide_render=true;
rerun=false. This object is excluded from masks and exports. The cleanup log has
an additional frame-corner cleanup entry on the fresh reconstruction; final
geometry hashes match. These are recorded rather than corrected in this cycle.

## Rerun procedure used

1. Extract Tesla.zip into a separate working directory, rejecting traversal.
   Omit old log/pycache files. Compare every delivered manifest entry to the
   existing source before executing scripts. Preserve original outputs here.
2. Open its supplied blend with Blender 5.2.2 LTS and run setup_reference,
   build_cage, build_surfaces, validate_silhouette, in that order. Every Blender
   invocation uses `--background` and `--python-exit-code 1`.
3. Check the blockout report's silhouette_pass before continuing. Then open its
   saved blend and run build_details, refine_final, fit_lamp_returns, presentation,
   audit_geometry, inspect_surface, render_matcap, render_validation,
   finalize_scene, validate_silhouette in that order.
4. Inspect the real studio, reflection, matcap and orthographic renders. Run the
   unchanged record_surface_review.py with ordinary Python. Reopen the saved
   blend and run export_glb.py in Blender, then verify_glb.py and build_viewer.py
   with ordinary Python.
5. Launch an isolated hidden/headless Edge instance on localhost:9333 using its
   own workspace user-data directory. Run test_viewer.mjs with Node. The first
   sandboxed browser attempt exited before Page.enable; the identical test
   passed when the local browser check ran outside the sandbox under approved
   execution. Close only the owned isolated browser afterward.
6. Run unchanged finalize_delivery.py in the isolated copy. Verify generated
   manifest, source/review/export bindings and actual embedded GLB bytes.
7. Reopen original and rebuilt blends read-only to capture scene inventories:
   object IDs/types/collections/parents/transforms, mesh vertex/face hashes,
   curve/control-handle hashes, camera settings, units and source digests. Never
   save over either file during inspection. Copy outputs here and compare them.

Execution transcripts are in `rerun/execution/`. The temporary working and
browser directories are ignored under `.preview/`; production scripts, original
Tesla model, exports and original delivery manifest were not modified.

The delivered archive is identified by SHA-256
`156bd5ab0353a266e4362f282ecaac11cc7b243ae742f79eb95fd781a9aa808d`.
Source reference hashes and actual decoded dimensions are in each validation
reference inventory. Reference scale remains the existing assumed 4.8 m length;
no new dimensional assumption was introduced.

Future generic regression must compare against this fixture's better current
metrics as well as the minimum thresholds, wheel centers, dimensions, semantic
structure, geometry integrity and actual browser behavior. Do not overwrite the
baseline to accept a regression.
